data.name: DreadStar: The Quest for Revenge
data.detailed_description:
Join us on Discord!


Acerca do jogo




A retro mix of a shoot 'em up gameplay and RPG elements, DreadStar: The Quest for Revenge is inspired by Tyrian, Raiden, Donpachi and other classic games. Fast-paced with a primary focus on gunplay rather than bullet hell, DreadStar gives you incremental ways of not only pushing through content, but also improving your ship and its loadout (such as experience, leveling and skill points).

If you’re struggling with a sector, you can warp over to Redbeard’s Burrow to spend credits, upgrade your ship and return to where you failed. From Gauss Cannons to Lazer Beams, Hadron Exploders to weapon cooling - ship improvements are key to not only choosing your playstyle but progressing through harder difficulties.

With its 4:3 display and CRT mode, to its multiple difficulty settings that offer replayability across its 6 sectors, DreadStar provides an authentic retro experience.





  • Fast shoot 'em up gameplay with epic boss fights.
  • 4 different ships and 10 different weapons to annihilate your opponents.
  • Tons of other customization options from armors and engines to shields and special items.
  • Gain experience and skill points to incrementally improve your ship’s strength.
  • 6 replayable sectors filled with unique enemies, bosses and minibosses.
  • 3 difficulty settings for every sector, to improve both your skill and your ship.
  • Hand-crafted pixel art graphics, cutscenes and animations.
  • Chiptune soundtrack by Yerzmyey, created on Amiga, Atari-ST and ZX Spectrum computers.
  • A 4:3 display and CRT mode for an authentic retro experience.

data.short_description: Will you have what it takes to avenge your father, defeat the evil DreadSkull and save the galaxy? Collect gems and customize your ship to get through six replayable sectors, annihilate your foes and fight epic bosses in this classic styled pixel art shoot'em'up with RPG progression.

reviews.review:
[quote][url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/32732116-IndieGems/]Follow our curator page: [b]IndieGems[/b] if you like and want to see more reviews like this one.[/url][/quote]

Classic arcade-style shoot-em-up games are rather challenging and rely on pattern-learning and proper execution. [i]DreadStar: The Quest for Revenge[/i] follows in suit with a few short levels and varied bosses to keep the game feeling rather fresh at every point. Three different difficulty options are available for each stage, progressively unlocked. The game does give a bit more leniency from the traditional shoot-em-up game with its leveling-up system and purchasable ship-modifications that are sometimes needed to get the player over the hump.

[h1]The Short Game[/h1]
The game only has 6 stages, with one unlocking after another during your first time running through. There are unique bosses in every stage, one mid and one final boss, except for the final stage, which just has one boss. The final stage is the shortest, while the others are comparable in length. Nothing is particularly long. The only time you would have a drawn-out level is if you take a long time getting through the bosses, otherwise things you don't kill just move out of the way at a steady pace.

There is not much of a story, just like the classic arcade game, where you get a few lines and off you are killing bunches of enemies. This is the same and the game even offers a happy ending if you are careful in looking for clues on how to get it. For me, it was playing and replaying until I found out how to do it.

[h1]The Crutch[/h1]
Unlike other shoot-em-ups, you will have 0 in-level upgrades/power ups. Instead you will gain experience to level up, giving you points to allow you some permanent stat boosts. Your experience will accumulate whether you live or die through the mission, so you can just keep dying in the beginning and be able to accumulate enough for a few simple upgrades to get you through if you are stuck. The leveling up does get harder requiring more experience later on, so the process slows down.

In addition, you can visit RedBeard's to purchase a bunch of different build-altering weapons, shields, engines, hulls, and special items. All of these are permanent purchases and do not ever need replacement. Your hull does get damaged so you will need to repair between battles, unless you buy a self-repairing model. I relied on the level-up stat boosts and the shop purchases heavily to make it through the game, especially the Betelgeuse level on Brutal difficulty. I won't try to count how many times I died testing different builds and trying to find the best one for this level/difficulty combination.

One thing to really keep in mind if you are short on money [spoiler]is that if you have an auto-repairing hull, you can farm in-game currency by playing and just warping out of a level if you cannot make it to the end. If you take damage, your hull will repair itself instead of needing to be repaired. This may come in handy for those who have trouble getting past certain sections and just need some extra money to buy the upgrades needed.[/spoiler]

Another trick I learned (along the same lines) [spoiler]is that the shop will readily buy back anything you are not using at full-price, so you can recycle items/money at 0 losses, especially with a self-repairing hull.[/spoiler]

[h1]The Achievements Grind[/h1]
Most of the achievements will unlock as you play, but the level 30 and level 40 achievements I had to grind for after completing the whole game on all difficulty levels and then just playing on for experience points and level-ups. I only found out towards the end that you can tune the experience-gain up to 150% in the options menu, so that could have helped me get through the final grind a bit easier.

As for the Mega Happy End achievement, you just need to pay a little bit of attention and eventually you will see how.

[h1]Controls[/h1]
You can remap controls on your keyboard or controller. I used a controller to play the game, and I used my mouse in-between levels. The controller moves the mouse cursor instead of preset selections, making the between-level upgrading/shopping a bit awkward.

[h1]Graphics[/h1]
Nice pixel art and quite unique levels to give a fresh feel in each part of the game. You can play with the retro-style scanlines in place as well to get even more of that arcade feel.

[h1]Music & Sounds[/h1]
Music got a bit repetitive, especially playing some levels on repeat many times trying to get through. The sound effects are too loud and jarring at times, especially those from the secondary weapons. [strike]There is not a separate sound effects volume adjustment, only one for overall volume and a toggle to turn the music off. Hopefully this will be fixed soon.[/strike]

[h1]Audience[/h1]
Traditional shoot-em-up fans will definitely have a good time with this game. Though everyone's experience will vary based on experience with this type of game. It started off for me seemingly rather difficult even on the normal difficulty, until I realized that I could take advantage of the two tips I provided above, and the game flowed better.

I would say that in terms of difficulty, it's moderately difficult if you want to get through all of the sectors on the most difficult settings.

[h1]Pricing[/h1]
$9.99 US seems a bit much for a game that has only 6 levels, each one taking a handful of minutes. It took me about 4 hours of intermittent playing to get through the normal difficulty, with many deaths and warping out, trying to use different builds to advance. Overall it took me a little under 14 hours total to grind through the last of the achievements. (I didn't know about the experience gain slider in the options until I had already finished.)

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
[i]DreadStar: The Quest for Revenge[/i] is a pretty fun shoot-em-up with challenging levels that requires you to learn the patterns and use your best judgement to get through. Or you can stumble through it like me through a lot of trial-and-error and repeatedly failing, resulting in enough experience gain that I could upgrade my stats and move on.

The game could use some improvements and I did find a couple of bugs that were sporadically appearing, but since the levels are so short, I didn't mind resetting and redoing things as needed. [strike]The biggest thing for me that I wanted to see was a simple sound effect volume adjustment that's separate from the music volume.[/strike] (fixed) A lot of times when I was chatting with friends while playing and Shift+Tab to the Steam overlay, I saw a lot of lag and unresponsiveness, sometimes it was difficult to return to the game from there. So just be aware of that, you might want to avoid the Steam overlay while playing this game.

It was fun for me overall, but your experience will definitely vary. It's not for everyone, that's for sure. But check it out if you are looking for some old-school shoot-em-up action and feel.

Score: 7/10
